content: Intestinal complications may include bowel obstruction, gastrointestinal bleeding, anorexia, constipation, weight loss, hepatitis, jaundice, eosinophilic enteritis, and hepatomegaly (enlarged liver). Ocular effects can involve diminished vision. Nervous system-related symptoms may include dizziness, drowsiness, fatigue, headache, giddiness, neuralgia, and taste disturbances. Psychiatric effects may manifest as depression secondary to skin discoloration. Laboratory findings may show elevated levels of albumin, serum bilirubin, and AST (SGOT), eosinophilia, and hypokalemia. Ocular complications may also include maculopathy, specifically bull’s eye retinopathy. Other systemic effects may include splenic infarction, thromboembolism, anemia, cystitis, bone pain, edema, fever, lymphadenopathy, and vascular pain. The drug is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to clofazimine or any of its excipients. Skin dryness and ichthyosis may occur; applying oil to the skin may help alleviate these effects. The drug is classified as Pregnancy Category C, meaning it crosses the human placenta. Infants born to women who received the drug during pregnancy have been observed to have deeply pigmented skin at birth. The drug is distributed in human breast milk and should not be administered to breastfeeding women unless clearly indicated. Clofazimine is highly lipophilic and tends to accumulate predominantly in fatty tissues and cells of the reticuloendothelial system, being taken up by macrophages throughout the body. The drug has a half-life of approximately 70 days at steady state. Excretion is negligible in urine, with small amounts found in feces, bile, sputum, sebum, and sweat. It is recommended to take the drug with meals to enhance absorption. The above information is provided for general informational and educational purposes only. Individual treatment plans may vary, and formulary information is subject to change. Always consult the applicable healthcare provider for the most current and accurate information.
